steps.step: roundtable spoke in the task thread

plan.description: RoomSync is a booking system for shared resources like meeting rooms and equipment, building directly on the REST API, auth, and booking-flow experience you showed in your capstone project. You'll design a relational data model for resources and bookings, build a REST API with JWT authentication, implement conflict detection so double-bookings can't happen, write automated tests (pytest, building on your URL shortener work), set up CI with GitHub Actions, and put together a simple client plus a deployed demo. Along the way we'll also weave in some web security basics (input validation, auth hardening) and cloud deployment practices, since those are areas you're keen to grow in.
plan.big_task: RoomSync Foundations: Repo, Environment, and First Endpoint

subtasks.title: Repo setup and project scaffolding
subtasks.description: Create the RoomSync GitHub repo with a sensible structure (app/, tests/, .gitignore, requirements.txt or pyproject.toml). Initialize a FastAPI app skeleton and a Docker-based local Postgres setup (e.g. docker-compose.yml). Done when: the repo exists with an initial commit history (not one giant commit), the FastAPI app runs locally with `uvicorn`, and Postgres starts via docker-compose and is reachable from the app config.

subtasks.title: Health check endpoint
subtasks.description: Implement a GET /health endpoint that returns a 200 status and confirms the API is up and can connect to the database (e.g. runs a trivial query). Done when: hitting /health locally returns a JSON response like {"status": "ok", "db": "connected"}, and you've captured a screenshot or curl output showing this working.

subtasks.title: Data model design for resources and bookings
subtasks.description: Design the relational schema for this week's scope: a `resources` table (e.g. id, name, type, location) and a `bookings` table stub (id, resource_id, start_time, end_time, created_by) with appropriate foreign keys, even though bookings CRUD comes next week. Use SQLAlchemy models and Alembic (or similar) for migrations. Done when: migrations run cleanly against the local Postgres instance, the schema is documented in a short ERD or schema diagram, and both tables exist when you inspect the DB.

subtasks.title: CRUD endpoints for the Resource model
subtasks.description: Implement full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) REST endpoints for the `resources` entity using FastAPI and Pydantic schemas for request/response validation. Done when: you can create, list, retrieve by id, update, and delete a resource via curl or Postman, and you've included basic input validation (e.g. required fields, sensible types) to catch malformed requests.

subtasks.title: Automated tests and README write-up
subtasks.description: Write pytest tests covering the health check and each Resource CRUD endpoint (happy path plus at least one validation/error case), building on your URL shortener testing experience. Then write a README explaining what RoomSync is, how to set up the environment (Docker, env vars), how to run migrations, how to start the app, and how to run the tests. Done when: `pytest` passes locally with all new tests green, and a teammate could follow the README alone to get the app running from a fresh clone.
